title: Misteri e indagini
sub: Modali al passato - fare ipotesi in riunione e il report
grammar: Modali al passato: must have, might have, can't have, should have, needn't have
situation: Riunione: analizzare un problema e fare ipotesi

lessons.title: Deve essere stato... non può essere stato...
lessons.intro: Come si ragiona sul passato quando non si è certi: deduzioni, ipotesi, critiche e cose inutili fatte. Sono i modali al passato, essenziali per riunioni, indagini e conversazioni su ciò che è successo.

steps.title: Deduzioni sul passato: must, can't, might
steps.body:
Per dire che cosa **pensi** sia successo, in base a indizi, si usa **modale + have + participio**. Il modale indica quanto sei sicuro:
- **must have** = sono quasi certo che sia successo
- **may / might / could have** = è possibile
- **can't / couldn't have** = sono quasi certo che NON sia successo

Per la negazione di certezza si usa **can't have**, non «mustn't have»: l'opposto di must have è can't have.
**might not have** significa «forse non è successo» (non è certo come can't have).

**Errori tipici degli italiani**: «must to have», «must have came» (dopo have serve il participio) e «he must have to»: have è l'ausiliare, non un verbo di obbligo.
ex: The lights are on, so he must have come back.
Le luci sono accese, quindi dev'essere tornato.
She can't have written this: her English isn't good enough.
Non può averlo scritto lei: il suo inglese non è abbastanza buono.
It might have been a power cut.
Potrebbe essere stata una mancanza di corrente.

steps.title: Forma continua e deduzioni su un periodo
steps.body:
Se l'azione era in corso o è durata a lungo, usa **have been + -ing**:
- She must have been working all night. (ha lavorato per ore: continua)
- They can't have been waiting long.

Ma attenzione: se parli del **presente** si usa il modale + infinito semplice: He must be tired (ora). Confronta:
- He **must be** at home. (adesso)
- He **must have been** at home. (prima)

Nella lingua dei verbali e delle riunioni si ammorbidisce con **It seems that... / It appears that... / There must have been...**
ex: He must have been driving too fast.
Dev'essere andato troppo veloce.
There must have been a mistake.
Dev'esserci stato un errore.

steps.title: Critica e rimpianto: should have, could have
steps.body:
Con lo stesso schema (modale + have + participio) si esprime un giudizio su un'azione passata:
- **should have / ought to have** = era la cosa giusta da fare, ma non è stata fatta
- **shouldn't have** = è stato un errore farlo
- **could have** = era possibile, ma non è successo (rimprovero o occasione persa)

You should have called. (Non hai chiamato: errore.)
You shouldn't have called. (Hai chiamato: non andava fatto.)
You could have called. (Era possibile: perché no?)
ex: You should have told me earlier.
Avresti dovuto dirmelo prima.
We shouldn't have taken that road.
Non avremmo dovuto prendere quella strada.
You could have called me!
Avresti potuto chiamarmi!

steps.title: Needn't have o didn't need to?
steps.body:
Entrambi significano «non era necessario», ma con una differenza importante:
- **needn't have + participio**: l'ho fatto, ma non serviva. I needn't have hurried. (Ho fatto in fretta, inutilmente.)
- **didn't need to + verbo base**: non era necessario; non sappiamo se l'ho fatto. I didn't need to hurry, so I walked.

Con didn't need to, se il contesto dice che l'azione è avvenuta, equivale a needn't have. Con needn't have, invece, l'azione è sempre avvenuta.
ex: We needn't have booked a table: the restaurant was empty.
Non serviva prenotare: il ristorante era vuoto.
She didn't need to wait, so she left.
Non doveva aspettare, perciò se n'è andata.

steps.s: The lights were off, so they ___ at home.
steps.it: Le luci erano spente, quindi non potevano essere a casa.
steps.why: Deduzione negativa sul passato: can't have been. «Mustn't have» non si usa per dedurre.

steps.s: There's a wet umbrella in the hall. It ___ raining when she arrived.
steps.why: Indizio forte, azione passata: must have been.

steps.s: You ___ me you were ill! I would have helped.
steps.why: Rimprovero su un'azione non fatta: should have + participio.

steps.s: We ___ hurried: the train was twenty minutes late.
steps.why: Abbiamo fatto fretta senza necessità: needn't have + participio.

opts: She can't have written this email: she doesn't speak Spanish.
She mustn't have written this email: she doesn't speak Spanish.
She can't wrote this email: she doesn't speak Spanish.
steps.why: Per dedurre che qualcosa è impossibile nel passato: can't have + participio.

steps.q: Che cosa significa «I needn't have brought an umbrella»?
opts: Ho portato l'ombrello, ma non serviva.
Non ho portato l'ombrello perché non serviva.
Non avrei dovuto portare l'ombrello perché era vietato.
steps.why: Needn't have + participio: l'azione è stata compiuta inutilmente.

steps.q: Metti il verbo tra parentesi alla forma giusta
steps.s: The dog ___ (might / eat) the cake: there are crumbs by its bed.
steps.why: Possibilità sul passato: might + have + participio (eaten).

answers: You should have let me know
You should have told me earlier
You should have warned me earlier
You ought to have warned me
You ought to have told me
You ought to have let me know
You ought to have told me earlier
You ought to have warned me earlier
steps.why: Rimprovero sul passato: should have / ought to have + participio.

steps.s1: I'm sure Tom took the wrong bus.
steps.why: Deduzione quasi certa sul passato: must have + participio.

steps.s1: It's impossible that she saw us: she was in Paris.
steps.s2: She ___ us: she was in Paris.
steps.why: Impossibilità sul passato: couldn't have + participio.

steps.s1: It was a mistake to leave so late.
steps.why: Critica su un'azione compiuta: shouldn't have + participio.

steps.s1: It wasn't necessary for us to take a taxi, but we did.
steps.why: Azione compiuta ma inutile: needn't have + participio.

steps.s1: Perhaps the thief got in through the window.
steps.s2: The thief ___ in through the window.
steps.why: Possibilità sul passato: might + have + participio.

steps.s: He must to have forgotten the password.
answers: He must have forgotten the password
steps.why: Dopo un modale non c'è to: must have + participio.

steps.s: They mustn't have seen the sign, otherwise they wouldn't have parked there.
answers: They can't have seen the sign, otherwise they wouldn't have parked there
They couldn't have seen the sign, otherwise they wouldn't have parked there
steps.why: Per dedurre che qualcosa non è successo si usa can't / couldn't have, non mustn't have.

steps.s: You needn't to have waited for me.
answers: You needn't have waited for me
You need not have waited for me
steps.why: Needn't è un modale: niente to, solo needn't have + participio.

steps.it: Deve aver lavorato tutta la notte.
steps.en: She must have been working all night

steps.it: Non possono aver saputo del piano.
steps.en: They can't have known about the plan
alts: They couldn't have known about the plan

lessons.title: Misteri, scienza, indagini
lessons.intro: Il lessico di chi indaga, formula ipotesi e verifica i fatti: serve per leggere articoli scientifici e di cronaca e per partecipare a una riunione in cui si cerca la causa di un problema.

ex: The torn letter was the first clue.
La lettera strappata fu il primo indizio.
words.note: Anche: I haven't got a clue = non ne ho idea.

ex: Our hypothesis is that the signal comes from the lab next door.
La nostra ipotesi è che il segnale arrivi dal laboratorio accanto.
Doctors have ruled out a heart problem.
I medici hanno escluso un problema cardiaco.
The council has promised to look into the complaints.
Il comune ha promesso di indagare sui reclami.
words.note: Pv inseparabile: look into the matter.

ex: The disappearance of the files remains baffling.
La scomparsa dei file resta incomprensibile.
words.note: Il participio baffled descrive chi è sconcertato.

ex: Someone had tampered with the lock.
Qualcuno aveva manomesso la serratura.
It can't be a coincidence that both machines failed on the same day.
Non può essere una coincidenza che entrambe le macchine si siano guastate lo stesso giorno.
There is no conclusive proof that the water was polluted.
Non c'è una prova decisiva che l'acqua fosse inquinata.
The new data cast doubt on the original theory.
I nuovi dati mettono in dubbio la teoria iniziale.

words.it: andare a fondo di, scoprire la verità su
ex: We are determined to get to the bottom of this.
Siamo decisi ad andare a fondo di questa faccenda.
The findings of the study will be published next month.
I risultati dello studio saranno pubblicati il mese prossimo.
words.note: Quasi sempre al plurale in questo senso.

ex: Engineers traced the fault to a loose cable.
Gli ingegneri hanno fatto risalire il guasto a un cavo allentato.
words.note: Anche nome: not a trace of = nessuna traccia di.

ex: Her explanation sounded perfectly plausible.
La sua spiegazione sembrava del tutto plausibile.
The idea that the bridge was built by aliens is far-fetched.
L'idea che il ponte sia stato costruito dagli alieni è inverosimile.

pairs: get to the bottom of it

steps.s: The police are ___ the disappearance of the painting.
steps.why: Look into = indagare. Look after = prendersi cura; look up = cercare (una parola).

steps.s: The results ___ doubt on the earlier theory.
steps.why: La collocazione è cast doubt on.

steps.s: Her story sounds a bit far-___ : I can't believe it.
steps.why: Far-fetched = poco credibile.

steps.s: The test results were ___ , so we had to repeat the experiment.
steps.why: Serve l'aggettivo negativo: conclude -> inconclusive.

opts: Una semplice coincidenza, senza altra spiegazione
steps.why: Coincidence = due fatti simultanei senza relazione tra loro.

lessons.title: Il caso del violino scomparso
lessons.intro: Un articolo da rivista su un furto d'arte risolto grazie a un dettaglio minuscolo. Segui le deduzioni di chi indaga: le domande chiedono di capire che cosa implica il testo, non solo che cosa dice.

steps.title: The case of the vanishing violin
steps.text:
When the curator of a small museum in northern Italy opened the display case one Monday morning, she knew at once that something was wrong. The violin, an eighteenth-century instrument worth almost two million euros, had gone. The alarm had not sounded, the door had not been forced and the cameras showed nothing unusual. The police, understandably, were baffled.

The first theory was that the thief must have been an insider. Only four members of staff had keys, and the alarm code had been changed only a week earlier. Yet all four had solid alibis, and none of them seemed to have any money problems. Detectives interviewed visitors, checked the delivery records and even looked into a former employee who had left the museum on bad terms. Nothing came of it.

It was a forensic scientist, Dr Elena Marchetti, who changed the direction of the investigation. Examining the glass case under a microscope, she noticed a thin line of fine, pale dust around the lock. It was not the grey dust of the museum's old floors; it was plaster. "That told me something simple," she said later. "Whoever opened the case had been in contact with building work, and the museum itself had not been decorated for years." The records showed, however, that a team of builders had repaired the ceiling of the neighbouring room three weeks before the theft.

The builders were checked one by one. Most could be ruled out quickly. One, however, had worked at the museum for only two days, under a name that turned out to be false. The agency that had sent him had no record of him either. On the day he left, he had apparently asked a colleague, quite casually, how the alarm system worked. At the time, nobody thought anything of it.

Even so, the evidence was circumstantial, and Dr Marchetti insisted on caution. "A coincidence can look very convincing," she said. "You must never fall in love with your own theory." Further tests on the plaster, together with a fingerprint found on the underside of the case, finally linked the man to the scene. He was arrested at a railway station three months later, and the violin was found, undamaged, wrapped in a bedsheet in a rented garage.

The case has since become a favourite example in police training courses. It shows, the instructors say, that investigations are rarely solved by sudden flashes of genius. More often they depend on patient attention to small, unglamorous details, and on the willingness to say "I don't know yet" until the facts allow a better answer.

qs.q: Why was the theft so puzzling at first?
opts: The violin was not worth much.
There were no signs of a break-in.
The cameras showed the thief clearly.
qs.why: «The alarm had not sounded, the door had not been forced».

qs.q: Why did detectives first suspect someone working at the museum?
opts: Only a few people had keys.
The cameras showed a member of staff.
qs.why: «Only four members of staff had keys»; gli altri indizi non sono veri nel testo.

qs.q: What happened when the detectives investigated the staff?
opts: They found the violin in a staff room.
They discovered that one person had lied.
They found nothing to link anyone to the theft.
qs.why: «all four had solid alibis... Nothing came of it».

qs.q: What did Dr Marchetti find near the lock?

opts: It suggested a link with recent building work.
It showed that the case had been cleaned.
It proved that the museum floors were old.
qs.why: Il gesso collega la serratura ai lavori edili nella stanza accanto.

qs.q: What made one of the builders suspicious?
opts: He asked for a high salary.
He had worked there for years.
He left the museum at night.
qs.why: «under a name that turned out to be false».

qs.q: What does Dr Marchetti mean by «You must never fall in love with your own theory»?
opts: Scientists should never share their ideas.
A coincidence is always more likely than a plan.
An attractive theory may be wrong, so it must be tested.
Theories are less important than luck.
qs.why: Il contesto: «A coincidence can look very convincing»; serve cautela e verifica.

qs.q: According to the instructors, investigations are usually solved by ___ .
qs.why: «they depend on patient attention to small, unglamorous details».

steps.q: Nel testo, «could be ruled out» significa:
steps.why: Rule out = escludere una possibilità o un sospettato.

steps.s: The evidence was ___ : it suggested he was guilty but did not prove it.
steps.why: Prova indiziaria: circumstantial evidence.

steps.s: The thief had not forced the door, so the alarm had never ___ .
steps.why: L'allarme che suona: the alarm sounds / sounded.

lessons.title: Perché le vendite sono crollate?
lessons.intro: Una riunione di lavoro in cui quattro colleghi cercano la causa di un calo di vendite. Ascolta come avanzano ipotesi, le scartano e si mettono d'accordo sul da farsi.

steps.title: A sales problem
steps.it: Ascolta la riunione. Puoi riascoltarla e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Right, thanks for coming, everyone. As you know, sales through the app dropped by almost thirty per cent last week, and we need to understand why. Any ideas?
My first thought was the update. It went live on Tuesday, so the timing is suspicious. Something must have gone wrong in the checkout.
Possible. Priya, you looked at the logs, didn't you?
I did. And honestly, it can't have been the update. The checkout error rate is exactly the same as before. People are reaching the payment page, but fewer of them are completing the purchase.
So it could be the payment provider. They might have changed something on their side.
I rang them this morning. They say nothing has changed, though I'm not sure I believe them.
Hmm. What about the competition? Daniel?

Well, I checked. Our main rival launched a big discount campaign on Monday. That may well have taken some of our customers. Mind you, it doesn't explain why people leave at the payment stage, does it?
No, that's true. Unless it's the delivery costs. We raised the free-delivery limit from thirty to fifty pounds last month. People might have been surprised by the extra charge at the last moment.
That would make sense. Customers must have seen the shipping fee only on the final screen.
In which case we should have told them earlier. And to be honest, we needn't have changed the limit at all. It saved us very little.

Right. Let's not jump to conclusions, but I like that theory. Priya, can you compare the abandonment rates before and after the change? Karim, please test the app on three different phones, in case there's a display problem. And Daniel, find out exactly what our rival's offer includes. We'll meet again on Friday.

qs.q: Sales through the app fell by about ___ per cent.
Why did Karim suspect the update?
opts: It had been released at about the same time as the drop.
It was the only change made that month.
It had cost a lot of money.
qs.why: «It went live on Tuesday, so the timing is suspicious».

qs.q: What did Priya's check of the logs show?
opts: The update had caused many errors.
qs.why: «it can't have been the update. The checkout error rate is exactly the same».

qs.q: What does Daniel say about the competitor's campaign?
opts: It may explain some lost customers but not the whole problem.
qs.why: «That may well have taken some of our customers. Mind you, it doesn't explain why people leave at the payment stage».

opts: Customers were surprised by delivery charges.
The payment page has a bug.
qs.why: Il limite per la consegna gratuita è salito da 30 a 50 sterline.

qs.q: What does Daniel think about the change to the free-delivery limit?
opts: It was copied from a rival.
qs.why: «we needn't have changed the limit at all. It saved us very little».

qs.q: What is Karim asked to do?
opts: Test the app on several phones
qs.why: «Karim, please test the app on three different phones».

steps.en: It can't have been the update: the error rate is exactly the same as before.
steps.it: Non può essere stato l'aggiornamento: la percentuale di errori è identica a prima.

steps.en: People might have been surprised by the extra charge at the last moment.
steps.it: Le persone potrebbero essere rimaste sorprese dal costo extra all'ultimo momento.

steps.en: Let's not jump to conclusions, but I like that theory.
steps.it: Non saltiamo alle conclusioni, ma questa teoria mi piace.

lessons.title: In riunione: cercare la causa
lessons.intro: Un problema, nessuna certezza e quattro colleghi: come fare ipotesi con il giusto grado di cautela, contestare un'idea con garbo e tenere in carreggiata la discussione.

steps.title: Fare ipotesi con cautela
steps.body:
In riunione conviene non presentare le ipotesi come fatti. Il grado di sicurezza si regola così:
- **Molto probabile**: It must have been..., It's highly likely that..., There's a good chance that...
- **Possibile**: It could / might be..., It may well have been..., Perhaps / Possibly...
- **Poco probabile**: It's unlikely that..., It can't have been..., I doubt that...

Frasi per introdurre un'ipotesi: **My guess is that...**, **I suspect that...**, **One possible explanation is...**, **It would seem that...**
ex: My guess is that the delay was caused by a supplier.
Secondo me il ritardo è dovuto a un fornitore.
It may well have been a software error.
Potrebbe benissimo essere stato un errore del software.

steps.title: Dissentire con garbo e guidare la discussione
steps.body:
Per non rispondere con un secco «no»:
- **I'm not sure I agree.** / **I'm not convinced that...** = Non sono sicuro di essere d'accordo.
- **That's a fair point, but...** = È un buon punto, ma...
- **That doesn't quite add up.** = Non torna del tutto.
- **What makes you say that?** = Cosa te lo fa dire?

Per gestire la riunione: **Can I just come in here?** (intervenire), **Let's look at this from another angle.**, **Let's park that for now.** (mettiamolo da parte), **Shall we move on?**, **So, to sum up...**
ex: I'm not convinced that the update is to blame.
Non sono convinto che la colpa sia dell'aggiornamento.
That doesn't quite add up.
Questa cosa non quadra del tutto.

steps.title: Speculating in a meeting
steps.it: Scegli la risposta più adatta in una riunione (Tu).
lines: So why do you think the new product is getting so many returns?

opts: It may be down to the packaging: some customers might have received damaged boxes.
It is the packaging. I know it.
Maybe packaging, maybe not, who knows?

lines: I'm not sure. The returns forms mostly say "not as described".

opts: That's a good point. In that case, the description on the website could be misleading.
That's wrong. The forms are always wrong.
No, you can't be right about that.

lines: Could you check the product page before Thursday?

opts: Certainly. I'll compare it with the actual product and report back.
Why me? It's not my job.
I could, but I would rather not.

steps.why: Ipotesi formulata con modali di possibilità, accordo parziale, disponibilità concreta: il registro giusto per una riunione.

steps.title: Disagreeing politely
lines: It must have been human error. Someone probably entered the wrong figures.

opts: That's possible, but I'm not convinced. The figures were checked twice, so it seems unlikely.
Because the same error appears in three different reports. That doesn't quite add up.
I don't know, it's just my feeling.

lines: Fair enough. So what do you suggest?

opts: Perhaps we should check the software before we blame anyone.
We should find the person who did it.
I suggest we forget about it.

pairs: Questa cosa non quadra del tutto.

steps.it: Potrebbe essere stato un guasto elettrico.
steps.en: It could have been a power cut
My guess is that the delay was caused by a supplier.
steps.it: Secondo me il ritardo è dovuto a un fornitore.

steps.en: I'm not convinced that the update is to blame.
steps.it: Non sono convinto che la colpa sia dell'aggiornamento.

steps.en: Can I just come in here? That doesn't quite add up.
steps.it: Posso intervenire? Questa cosa non quadra del tutto.

steps.q: Your team's website crashed last night. In a meeting, suggest two possible causes and say what you would check first.
steps.it: Il sito della tua squadra è andato in tilt ieri sera. Proponi due cause possibili con il giusto grado di cautela e di' che cosa controlleresti per primo (almeno 4 frasi).
steps.model: My guess is that too many people visited the site at the same time, because we sent the newsletter yesterday afternoon. It might also have been a problem with the server: the engineers updated it on Monday. I doubt that it was a cyber attack, as we didn't see any strange activity. First, I'd check the traffic figures, and then I'd ask the engineers what changed.

lessons.title: Il report
lessons.intro: Scriverai un report in stile B2 First con titoli e raccomandazioni. Prima gli strumenti: struttura e frasi prudenti, poi qualche esercizio per scaldarti.

steps.title: Come si scrive un report
steps.body:
Il report del B2 First è rivolto a un destinatario preciso (un direttore, un insegnante) ed è **organizzato con titoli**. Registro neutro-formale, nessun saluto.
- **Introduction**: scopo del report (The aim of this report is to...).
- **Sezioni con titolo**: ognuna tratta un punto (Possible reasons, Findings...).
- **Recommendations**: proposte concrete (I would recommend that..., The school could...).
- **Conclusion**: sintesi in una frase.

Frasi utili: **It would seem that...**, **Most students said that...**, **It is unlikely that...**, **I would strongly recommend...**, **This would enable / allow...**. Evita le contrazioni e il tono troppo personale. I criteri sono sempre: contenuto, comunicazione, organizzazione, lingua.
ex: The aim of this report is to examine why attendance has dropped.
Lo scopo di questo report è esaminare perché la frequenza è calata.
I would recommend offering evening classes.
Raccomanderei di offrire lezioni serali.

steps.s: The ___ of this report is to explain why customers have complained.
steps.why: Nel report si dice: The aim / purpose of this report is to...

steps.s: I would ___ that the company introduces more flexible working hours.
steps.why: Recommend that + soggetto + verbo. Con suggest/advise la costruzione sarebbe diversa («suggest that», «advise someone to»).

steps.s: It would ___ that most students are satisfied with the teaching.
steps.why: It would seem / appear that = sembrerebbe che (tono formale e cauto).

steps.s: I recommend to introduce a shorter timetable.
answers: I recommend introducing a shorter timetable
I would recommend introducing a shorter timetable
I recommend that the school introduces a shorter timetable
I would recommend that the school introduces a shorter timetable
I recommend that we introduce a shorter timetable
I would recommend that we introduce a shorter timetable
I recommend that the school introduce a shorter timetable
I would recommend that the school introduce a shorter timetable
steps.why: Dopo recommend non si usa to + infinito: serve -ing oppure that + clausola.

steps.q: The manager of the language school where you study has asked students to write a report on why many students leave after their first term. Write your report, suggesting possible reasons and recommending improvements.
steps.it: Scrivi un report (140-190 parole) per il direttore della scuola: introduzione, sezioni con titolo (motivi possibili, raccomandazioni), conclusione. Usa almeno due modali di deduzione al passato.
checklist: Contenuto: ho proposto motivi possibili e raccomandazioni concrete
Comunicazione: registro neutro-formale, nessun saluto, niente contrazioni
Organizzazione: titoli, introduzione con lo scopo, conclusione
Lingua: ho usato almeno due modali di deduzione (must / might / can't have) e formule come It would seem that
Ho rispettato il numero di parole (140-190)
useful: The aim of this report is to...
It is unlikely that... was the main reason
steps.model:
Introduction
The aim of this report is to examine why a number of students leave the school after their first term and to suggest improvements.

Possible reasons
Many students must have found the timetable difficult, as most classes take place in the early evening, when people are tired after work. Several students also told me that the groups were too large. It is unlikely that the fees were the main problem, since they are lower than those of other schools. Some people might have left because they did not see enough progress.

Recommendations
Firstly, I would recommend offering a wider choice of class times, including weekend lessons. Secondly, the school could limit groups to twelve students. Finally, a short progress meeting after six weeks would help learners to see how much they have improved.

Conclusion
It would seem that the school has a good reputation but does not yet meet the needs of working adults. These changes would probably encourage more students to stay.

steps.q: Think of an unsolved mystery or a strange event. What do you think happened?
steps.it: Parla di un mistero irrisolto o di un evento strano e di' che cosa pensi sia successo, usando modali di deduzione al passato.
steps.model: The mystery I find most interesting is the Mary Celeste, the ship that was found with nobody on board. The crew can't have been attacked, because their belongings were still there. It might have been a storm, or the sailors may have feared that the ship was about to explode. In my view, they must have left in a hurry in the lifeboat, and then something went wrong.

steps.q: Describe a time when something went wrong at work or at home. What do you think caused it?
steps.it: Racconta un momento in cui qualcosa è andato storto e dì quali possono essere state le cause (almeno 4 frasi).
steps.model: Last week our internet stopped working for a whole day. It might have been a problem with the provider, but the neighbours were online, so it can't have been that. I think I must have unplugged the router while cleaning the room. I should have checked it first. Next time I'll look at the cables before calling anyone.

steps.title: A village mystery
steps.text: Residents of Eastwick woke up on Sunday to find that the village clock had stopped at 3.17. Nobody had heard anything during the night, so a power cut {1} the most likely explanation. But the engineer who {2} into it found nothing wrong. "It can't {3} been the electricity," she said, "because the church bells, which are on the same circuit, kept ringing all night." Some villagers think someone must {4} tampered with the mechanism, although the tower door was locked. For the moment the case remains {5} .

steps.title: A message from the lab
lines: Hello, this is Anita Pace from the lab. I've looked at the water samples from the lake. I'd say the fish can't have died because of pollution from the factory, as the levels of chemicals are perfectly normal. It might have been the heat: last week was unusually hot, and the oxygen in the water may have dropped sharply. I'm not certain yet, so please don't announce anything before I send the full report on Friday.

qs.q: What does Anita think about the factory?
opts: It is the most likely cause.
It is unlikely to be the cause.

qs.q: What might have caused the problem?
opts: A lack of oxygen caused by the heat

qs.q: What does she ask the listener to do?
opts: Wait for her report before saying anything
